messages:
maya: Heads-up: I want to shrink the rollout/pin manifest we keep in control-plane. We currently store lots of historical/ops fields that the runtime never reads. Proposal: a compact runtime-facing core + string-only annotations for everything else. Thoughts?
lucas: Sounds good in principle. Need to be careful about semantics we rely on for routing (eg hard vs soft affinity, fallback behavior). If we move anything non-obvious to annotations we might lose deterministic behavior.
sophia: Agreed with maya. My suggestion: core contains only fields used by the router/placement/fallback logic: schema_version, phase, affinity, priority, compatibility_hints, fallback_variant. All other metadata -> annotations. Keep annotations as string->string map.
kai: Quick sketch I threw together:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "1",
  "phase": "canary",
  "affinity": "soft",
  "priority": "50",
  "compatibility_hints": ["float16","kv-cache-v2"],
  "fallback_variant": "variant-b",
  "annotations": {"owner":"team-compute","runbook":"doc.link/abc"}
}
```
Note: priority is an int range 0-100, but annotations are strings. Router ignores unknown annotation keys.
jamie: Ops questions: how do we migrate existing manifests? Tenants have long-lived manifests, and some internal tooling expects older fields. We need a validator/migration playbook and backwards tolerance window.
lucas: Validator rules I think we should add: 1) schema_version required; 2) phase in {canary,stable,deprecated}; 3) affinity defaults to none if absent; 4) priority in 0..100; 5) annotations total size cap (4KB) to avoid abuse. Validator should be permissive about extra top-level keys for at least one major release.
maya: Good. Also we need to decide whether fallback_variant belongs in core. I vote yes: it's used at routing time and should not be buried in annotations.
sophia: +1 for fallback_variant in core. Also recommend adding an optional "deprecation_ts" (ISO8601 string) to core for quick checks when rollout state needs to age out. If you want ultra-minimal we can keep it out and push to annotations, but deprecation_ts is runtime-useful.
kai: Tradeoff: more core fields = faster runtime decisions but less flexibility long-term. I think deprecation_ts is okay as optional since we already do TTL checks. Keep core minimal and optional fields typed.
jamie: Console UX: we'll need a view that shows core fields prominently and an "annotations" expandable blob. Also docs on recommended annotation keys (owner, ticket, notes, rollout-id). We'll need to reserve some key prefixes like "rdw:" for internal keys.
maya: Security and tenants: annotations are string blobs but could contain URLs/keys. We should restrict annotation size and forbid sensitive keys by convention. Add policy to strip known secrets from annotations during ingestion.
deploy-bot: system: rollout-validator v0.9 observed new schema_version field in manifests for tenant alpha. Validator flagged unknown field "deprecated_internals" but accepted manifest on permissive mode.
lucas: Migration plan (short): 1) Validator permissive mode live for two releases. 2) Backfill: run script to convert common legacy fields into annotations or core where appropriate. 3) Enable strict validation behind feature flag; notify tenants with failing manifests and give 30-day window.
sophia: Also run a runtime canary: route a small percentage of traffic to router that reads only core+annotations-as-strings to confirm no behavior differences. If we detect drift, revert.
maya: Action items: - kai: implement runtime reader for new core fields and fallback logic (default affinity=none). - lucas: draft validator rules + migration script and a proforma tenant notification. - jamie/sophia: update Console docs and annotation key guidance; propose reserved prefixes. I'll write a tiny RFC summarizing this and include the example manifest above.
jamie: One more ops nit: add a checksum hash of manifest in core (sha1 hex) so we can cheaply detect changes in control-plane without inspecting annotations. Could be optional though.
kai: Fine with optional checksum. Runtime ignores if absent.
maya: Cool. We'll aim to announce the RFC on Monday and start validator permissive rollout mid-next-week. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
